answer.policy_title: Cigna Medical Coverage Policies – Musculoskeletal CMM-313: Hip Replacement/Arthroplasty
criteria_quotes: Total hip replacement is considered medically necessary for ANY of the following conditions when ALL of the associated criteria have been met.
The determination of medical necessity for the performance of hip resurfacing and hip replacement (partial or total) is always made on a case-by-case basis.

Non-Surgical Management ... [includes] relative rest/activity modification; weight loss; supervised physiotherapy modalities and therapeutic exercises; prescription and non-prescription medications; assistive devices; and/or intra-articular injections.
For individuals with significant medical conditions or comorbidities, the risk/benefit of hip arthroplasty procedures should be clearly documented in the medical record.
answer.appeal_deadline: January 30, 2027. The notice states that the appeal must be received within 180 days of August 3, 2026.
answer.submission_route: Call Cigna Customer Service at the telephone number on the back of the member ID card and request an appeal. Submit a completed Cigna Customer Appeal Request form or an appeal letter, the denial notice, and supporting medical records. The Cigna form states that the mailing address depends on the ID-card indicator: if the card says “GW - Cigna Network,” mail to Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188062, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8062; if it says “Cigna Network,” mail to Cigna Appeals Unit, P.O. Box 188011, Chattanooga, TN 37422-8011. The appeal letter should identify the request as a “Customer Appeal,” include reference number POC-E7809C09B9-10970, and specifically document the provider-directed conservative treatments attempted, their duration and results, current symptoms and functional limitations, relevant imaging, and the treating surgeon’s medical-necessity explanation.
answer.how_to_obtain_criteria: The governing policy is publicly available at the policy URL above. Cigna’s member appeal instructions also state that the applicable appeal process is determined by the member’s plan documents and that the member may call the number on the ID card for additional information. If Cigna applied additional plan-specific or clinical-review criteria not contained in CMM-313, request the complete criteria and review rationale in writing from Cigna, including the clinical-review guidelines used for reference POC-E7809C09B9-10970.

answer.notes: The policy states that coverage policies are guidance and that the applicable benefit-plan document supersedes them if there is a conflict. The publicly retrieved policy identifies the total-hip-replacement indication section and the required conservative-management categories, but the denial letter does not identify which underlying condition or which specific associated criterion was found deficient. The appeal should therefore ask Cigna to identify the exact criterion applied and address every applicable criterion.

Date of notice: 2026-08-03
Member: Jordan Brooks
Member ID: W789350798
Plan: Cigna (Commercial/ACA), state of Nebraska

Dear Jordan,

We reviewed the prior authorization request submitted by your provider for the following service:

    Requested service: Total hip replacement
    Procedure code (CPT): 27130

After review, this request is DENIED. Reason for determination: the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery.

This determination was made under the plan's applicable medical policy and clinical review criteria. You have the right to appeal this decision. Your appeal must be received within 180 days of the date of this notice (by 2027-01-30).

Reference number: POC-E7809C09B9-10970

Hip Resurfacing Arthroplasty (HRA) (also called metal- on-metal [MoM] hip resurfacing and hemi-resurfacing arthroplasty) a surgical technique that involves the removal of diseased cartilage and bone from the head of the femur and the replacement of the surface of the femoral head with a metal hemisphere that fits into a metal acetabular cup or into the acetabulum, respectively. This technique conserves femoral bone and maintains normal femoral loading and stresses. Because of this bone conservation, it may not compromise future total hip replacements. Hip resurfacing arthroplasty has been promoted as an alternative to total hip replacement for younger individuals. Hip resurfacing arthroplasty may be either a partial HRA (i.e., hemi-hip resurfacing, hemi-resurfacing, or femoral head resurfacing arthroplasty [FHRA]) or a total HRA.
